The core operator 'gradient expectation' formalizes how neural systems optimize beliefs through expected gradient ascent. It bridges cognitive science and machine learning by modeling the brain as a predictor that minimizes surprise. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian updating where belief states evolve according to likelihood-weighted gradients. In GSE, it enables dynamic policy adaptation by computing expected changes in belief under action sequences. The conjugate gradient descent kernel refines this process by ensuring efficient exploration of belief space, avoiding redundant search paths. The predictive neural network framework synthesizes these into a unified architecture where each layer computes expectations conditioned on prior beliefs, forming a hierarchy of abstraction. Failure modes include gradient explosion in deep layers and divergence in non-stationary environments. Dualities emerge between belief propagation and variational inference, and between policy iteration and gradient descent. These operators exhibit anti-symmetry under time-reversal, implying inherent directionality in belief evolution.
